ORDER M/s.S.R. Sumathy, learned counsel, takes notice for the first respondent and Mr.P. Sathish, learned Additional Government Pleader, takes notice for the second and third respondents.
With the consent of both parties, the Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. The limited prayer sought for in this Writ Petition is for a direction to the second respondent herein, to dispose of the application preferred by the petitioners dated 05.12.2022, within a stipulated time.

3. It is needless to point out that whenever an arbitration petition https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis is preferred before the concerned Authority, there is a duty cast on them to dispose of the same expeditiously.

Non -compliance of such a responsibility would amount to dereliction of duties and this Court would be justified in directing the authority to dispose of the said petition within a stipulated time, in exercise of its powers under Article 226 of Constitution of India.
4.

In the light of the above observations, there shall be a direction to the second respondent herein,
to dispose of the petitioners' arbitration petition dated 05.12.2022, if not already disposed of, after giving opportunity to the petitioners, as well as any other person who may be interested in the subject property, on its own merits and in accordance with law, within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. With the above direction, the Writ Petition stands ordered.
No costs.
